details.label: Summary
details.text: The risk of locally damaging wind gusts and hail may spread east of Severe Thunderstorm Watch 616 this evening, though a downstream watch is not expected

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Along an eastward-moving cold front, two clusters of loosely organized thunderstorms in Middle TN and eastern KY are tracking east-southeastward toward the eastern edge of Severe Thunderstorm Watch 616 this evening. Around 30-40 kt of midlevel west-northwesterly flow (per JKL/OHX VWPs) oriented perpendicular to the front will aid in the maintenance of these storms for the next hour or so -- before reaching the higher terrain. This will especially be the case into eastern TN -- where lower/middle 80s temperatures and upper 60s dewpoints remain in place. As a result, the risk of locally damaging wind gusts and hail may spread east of the watch. However, given the localized nature of the ongoing severe risk, a downstream watch is not expected

details.label: Most probable threats
details.text: MOST PROBABLE PEAK WIND GUST...55-70 MPH · MOST PROBABLE PEAK HAIL SIZE...UP TO 1.25 IN

details.label: Summary
details.text: Several clusters of strong to severe storms continue over portions of WW615. Damaging winds remain possible with these storms. Some risk may continue into parts of northwestern AL this evening

details.label: Discussion
details.text: As of 2330 UTC, regional radar showed several clusters of strong to severe storms ongoing across portions of WW615. The most intense of these clusters, located near the MS/TN border has produced recent measured severe gusts. This should continue across portions of southern TN and northern MS where moderate to large buoyancy and 25-35 kt of deep-layer shear are present and supporting more organized multicell clusters. High PWATS (2+ inches) and clustering will promote stronger downdrafts capable of damaging/isolated severe gusts. The primary severe risk appears most likely along the southwestern flank of the leading cluster across north-central MS where stronger low-level convergence along the existing outflow may preferentially support maintenance of the ongoing storms/new development this evening. However, some severe risk is possible east of WW615 into parts of northwestern AL this evening. However, the environment farther east is cooler and somewhat drier with less overall buoyancy. Weaker vertical shear with southward extent also casts some uncertainty on longevity. Regardless, enough buoyancy and steep low-level lapse rates likely exist to support an isolated damaging wind threat

details.label: Most probable threats
details.text: MOST PROBABLE PEAK WIND GUST...65-80 MPH · MOST PROBABLE PEAK HAIL SIZE...UP TO 1.25 IN
